name: Aegis YUSD
oneLiner: Aegis YUSD is a synthetic dollar backed by BTC in institutional custody and hedged with equal short COIN-M perpetuals; funding-rate yield goes to holders.
collateral: Bitcoin held in institutional custody (Fireblocks, Copper, CEFFU); delta-neutral hedge via COIN-M perpetual futures; funded by user deposits of USDT, USDC, or DAI converted to BTC
pegMechanism: Delta-neutral hedging: BTC spot long + COIN-M perpetual short; 1:1 redemption via Aegis Mint contract; funding rate yield distributed to registered YUSD holders; insurance fund backstop for extreme events

oracleRisk.summary: YUSD is issued against Aegis's pooled BTC spot and COIN-M hedge portfolio rather than borrower debt positions with oracle-triggered collateral liquidation.

branchApplicability.rationale: Aegis documents permissioned minting from deposited USDT, USDC, or DAI and pooled backing through BTC spot positions hedged with COIN-M perpetuals. The reviewed issuer materials do not describe borrower-specific debt, collateral-ratio thresholds, or a collateral liquidation branch for YUSD issuance.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The verified Ethereum YUSD source gives the owner addBlackList and removeBlackList authority. Its _update hook rejects transfers where either the sender or recipient is blacklisted, establishing a direct holder-level transfer restriction on the tracked token.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: SONG Safety Score V9 access review

mintAuthority.summary: YUSD's Ethereum minting is delegated to AegisMinting, where normal minting requires a whitelisted user/order plus trusted-signer signature and a 3/5 Safe controls the minter and default-admin role. Distinct BSC AegisMinting and Avalanche OFT authority paths are identified but not fully enumerated.

controls.label: AegisMinting

routeChecks.caps: mintLimit exists but current tuple read did not prove an active hard cap; admin can set mint limits

controls.evidence: YUSD.minter() returned AegisMinting. Sourcify source shows yusd.mint(...) in mint(), depositIncome(), and mintForCrossChain().

controls.label: Aegis admin Safe

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: Aegis admin Safe is owner/defaultAdmin for AegisMinting; reviewed as 3-of-5 with no modules and zero guard.
routeChecks.caps: Safe can administer mint limits and trusted-signer/cross-chain operator roles; the reviewed Ethereum trusted signer is configured by this Safe and CROSS_CHAIN_OPERATOR_ROLE is unassigned.

controls.evidence: AegisMinting.owner() and defaultAdmin() returned this Safe.

review.evidence: Direct reads and Sourcify source identify Ethereum AegisMinting as the active YUSD minter, with owner/default-admin control held by a 3/5 Safe. Follow-up verification 2026-07-20: AegisConfig (0x90ccf2c4b3dee7aeac9af5950a7c60f89af1db00).trustedSigner() = 0xb28c97e348c3078fc1f6fcc61b79c8a0da35008e, and config owner() = the same Safe. The BSC deployment has a distinct AegisMinting at 0x02bf8f0e..., and Avalanche uses a LayerZero OFT; their terminal minter, administrator, and upgrade-control chains are not fully represented here. The Accountable proof-of-reserves cadence and any prudential supervisor were not re-evidenced for this asset-level unresolved review.
unresolvedQuestions: Enumerate the BSC AegisMinting and Avalanche LayerZero OFT terminal minter, administrator, and upgrade authorities before treating YUSD as asset-wide scoreable.
Re-evidence the Accountable reconciliation cadence and any named prudential supervisor for YUSD before assigning reviewed profile-level values.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Aegis has YUSD deployments on Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Avalanche, and issuer route evidence identifies LayerZero-powered bridging to Avalanche. The bridge route is therefore treated as external lock/burn-and-mint infrastructure.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex bridge route review; Kimi P2 control cohort dc-3 (lead usds-sky) (2026-07-20)

routes.reviewNote: Native YUSD on Ethereum: minter() = AegisMinting 0xC4Df68e592245cA5202fE8b7C438d2b799820fc2 and owner() = the Aegis 3/5 Safe (verified on-chain 2026-07-20); no bridge representation.

Native YUSD on BSC: minter() = the BSC AegisMinting 0x02bf8f0e046f471709e578b1e633077096ce65cf (owner() = the same Aegis 3/5 Safe, aegisConfig() present, yusd() = this token; verified on-chain 2026-07-20).

Controller verified on-chain 2026-07-20: endpoint() of the Avalanche YUSD token returns the LayerZero EndpointV2 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c, so this deployment is the Aegis OFT and the OFT contract itself is the mint/burn authority for the representation.

reserveReview.reviewer: SOL-III Safety Score V9 reserve review
reserveReview.rationale: The 2026-07-15 Accountable snapshot split the adapter's scored reserve envelope between Copper and Fireblocks. Aegis describes that envelope as pooled BTC spot and short COIN-M perpetual positions, but the public snapshot does not split either custodian bucket into spot, derivative equity, margin, or venue exposures.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Accountable reserves_split values, normalized by the existing live-reserve adapter after excluding the separately reported insurance fund
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Both custody buckets contain an undisclosed mix of spot, hedge, margin, and counterparty exposures.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: The snapshot identifies the custody bucket but does not split its BTC spot, derivative, margin, and venue exposures.
